verdict.rationale: The Snyk CLI is documented to run in CI/CD pipelines under service accounts (headless), and there is a local MCP server built on the CLI that coding agents can prompt to scan. Snyk also documents exporting issues to Jira. However, the pack never documents machine-readable output such as JSON or SARIF flags: the only reporting evidence is a terminal report and an HTML plugin. Issue filing is also not tied to CLI scan results or to filtering for real findings. missing for 10: documented machine-readable CLI output (JSON/SARIF), an evidenced CLI-to-issue-tracker workflow, independent hands-on corroboration of agent-driven headless use.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can have an agent run a scan headlessly via the CLI, parse machine-readable results, and file issues for real findings

citations.quote: You can also run the CLI in your CI/CD pipeline.
This Organization-level role allows service accounts in CI/CD pipelines to run basic Snyk CLI commands.
The Snyk MCP Server is designed as a local MCP server, running on your system using the Snyk CLI to ensure local file access.
Track and export Snyk issues to your Jira project.
